answer: An operator running 109 keys thus burns for 109 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Because the inlet salt is published after the ember checkpoint, the jetty audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 96 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. That is 2 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
